messages.subject: Help MIMIC model
parts:
Hi, 

I'm new to SEM models but I need to use a MiMiC model in order to estimate the shadow economy in my country.

I'm using three/four indicators in the measurement equation, and another five to seven indicators in the Structural equation. I have 25 observations (annual data) for each variable and those variables are regular economic items (GDP, Labor Force, index of economic freedom, etc). The variables are expressed in percentage or in index. 

My problem is that I barely never get a convergence and if so it always have a negative variance somewhere.

Is it a problem of short sampling? Should I try quarterly date or panel data with other countries?

I have read the the PLS estimator is better to reach a solution. Does it Lavern support this estimator?

Thank you very much for your help.

Best rregards

Gonzalo

messages.subject: Re: Help MIMIC model
parts:
Gonzalo--
     Is this annual data for one country? If so, then your annual robservations are not independent observations. It is possible that nonconvergence is due not only to your small sample size but also to the nonindependence of observations. A time series approach would be more appropriate. A partial least squares path modeling approach would not be correct unless it also addressed the non-independence. A least squares ap[proach may well bypass some nonconvergence problems, but you will still have a small sample size, which will make you parameter estimates relatively unstable.
